summary:
The slice's SC-052 and SC-050 work holds in a real environment. Its startup-stall criterion (14) does not.

**SC-052, dead mapped share.** Two disposable Windows Sandbox runs (build 26100.9974) mapped Y: to a loopback SMB share and then silenced the server. LanmanServer, srv2 and srvnet were stopped and a listener on 445 accepts connections without answering. A separate IsReady probe on Y: never returned (it was still blocked after 8 and 7 minutes). Results with the real published exes:
- Report mode, slice: DrivePanel.buttons=1 (C:). HEAD's exe gave 0.
- Hooked (FsaWindowHook size mode), slice: 'drives in held=1909 / 1911 buttons=1 labels=1/1 ink=1/1'. DriveStatus changed about 1.9 s into the hold.
- Hooked, HEAD: 'refused ... the drive buttons did not come in within 20 s'.
- With Y: alive, both exes gave buttons=2.

**SC-050.**
- In the Sandbox, with C: labelled WD_BLACK, the slice's buttons read labels=2/2 and HEAD's read 0/2.
- An off-screen WPF layout of a Button showed the difference. With string content, WD_BLACK gets an AccessText with key 'B' and USB__DISK is drawn as 'USB_DISK'. With TextBlock content there is no AccessText, and both labels are drawn as written.
- B-007 on this PC: exit 0, labels=3/3 ink=3/3, real buttons '3 of 3' over 9 runs.

**Tests and rules.**
- StallStacks -SelfTest passed (14 fixtures).
- Fitness: all 107 rules hold.
- Full suite, run 1: 1213/1214. UnfinishedTests failed once; it passed 3 times in isolation and in run 2.
- Full suite, run 2: 1213/1214. AppArgumentTests failed only on my validation scratch: the HEAD copy, and the engine-written task.ps1 files under .taad-scratch/sandbox. It passed in run 1, before that scratch existed.

**Criterion 14 fails.** SL-002-StartupStallStacks.Tests.ps1 exits 1: scan 333.9 ms, RENDER-PATH, stalled=true. My own A/B of T-005 at 644 px gave HEAD scan 341.0 ms against the slice's 340.3 ms, so the stall is pre-existing and nothing in the slice causes it. It is still unmet, and O-013 was waived as N-018.

**O-014 is measured false, the same for HEAD and the slice.**
- With Y: alive, WM_CLOSE exited in 36 ms.
- With Y: dead, WM_CLOSE left the process alive after 120 s, down to 1 thread in Wait/Unknown, and Stop-Process had not finished 30 s later. This happened for the slice twice and for HEAD once.
- Report-mode shutdowns with the read stuck exited promptly in all 5 runs, 12–34 ms after the report.

**History.** No loop: each stage ran once.

checks.what: Full suite, run 1 (after republishing at HEAD)
checks.evidence: Failed 1, Passed 1213 of 1214, exit 1, 52 s. The failure was UnfinishedTests.StopsInTheSizeChecksMarkWhatAPendingCheckCouldChange(workers: 4). The slice changes no Core code, and git diff 3ab847c..HEAD touches neither src/FsAnalyser.Core nor UnfinishedTests.cs. The test passed 3 of 3 in isolation and in full run 2. It looks like a timing-flaky Core test, filed as backlog; it is not a slice defect.

checks.what: The flaky UnfinishedTests case in isolation, 3 times
checks.evidence: Passed 2/2 each time, exit 0, 3 of 3 runs.

Failed 1, Passed 1213, exit 1. AppArgumentTests.EveryScriptThatLaunchesTheAppIsListedAndQuotesByTheRule listed only validation scratch: .taad-scratch/sandbox/run-*/in/task.ps1 (the engine's copies of my Sandbox scripts) and .taad-scratch/validate/head/** (my HEAD copy). After the HEAD copy was removed, it still failed on the two sandbox task.ps1 files. It passed in run 1, before that scratch existed. Backlog item: the test walks untracked, non-ignored .taad-scratch. UnfinishedTests passed in this run.
PASSED: 14 fixtures, exit 0. Includes no-stall: NAMED, render-chain: RENDER-PATH and no-match: CANNOT-READ.
107 rules against 195 parsed files: every declared rule holds, including the two SL-002 rules. One rule matches no files (SL-089 c-drive-run.json). That gap predates this slice.

checks.what: B-007 on the final published exe, this PC's real drives (criteria 2, 7, 10)
checks.evidence: Exit 0 in 56 s. Lines read 'drives in ... added=26 buttons=29 labels=3/3 ink=3/3', then 'real drive buttons when the hold released, over 9 hooked runs: 3 of 3' and 'the hold released with the same real drive buttons in every hooked run, by both counts'.

checks.what: Sandbox run 1: report mode with a dead mapped Y:, slice exe vs HEAD exe (criterion 1)
checks.command: Sandbox network=true: share fsa, net use Y: \\127.0.0.1\fsa; stop LanmanServer, srv2 and srvnet; TcpListener on 445 that never answers; FsAnalyser.App.exe C:\work\tiny --report (out: .taad-scratch/sandbox/run-20261117-212042/out/log.txt)
checks.evidence: Live Y:, slice: DrivePanel.buttons=2, exited at +698 ms. Dead Y:, slice: DrivePanel.buttons=1, exited at +824 ms, code 0. Dead Y:, HEAD: DrivePanel.buttons=0, exited at +723 ms. The Y: IsReady probe started 21:25:33 and had not returned by 21:32:36. The listener logged a reconnect accept about every 62 s.

checks.what: Sandbox run 1: reading DriveStatus by UI Automation on a no-path launch
checks.command: UIAutomationClient FindFirst by ProcessId, inside the Sandbox
checks.evidence: Every read returned 'no-window'. The Sandbox runs as SYSTEM in session 0, the window was not visible (vis=False in run 2) and Process.MainWindowHandle was 0. So CloseMainWindow sent nothing. The 'STILL RUNNING' lines in run 1's GUI rows mean no close was sent; they are not a hang.

checks.what: Sandbox run 1: relabel C: with Set-Volume
checks.evidence: 'No MSFT_Volume objects found' on the Sandbox's C:. Run 2 used 'label C: WD_BLACK' instead, and DriveInfo then read label [WD_BLACK].

checks.what: Sandbox run 2: hooked report runs with Y: alive and C: labelled WD_BLACK (criteria 2, 10, 11)
checks.evidence: Slice: 'drives in ms=775 held=4 added=0 buttons=2 labels=2/2 ink=2/2', exit 0. HEAD: 'drives in ms=683 held=1 buttons=2 labels=0/2 ink=0/2'. The C: button with a WD_BLACK label has TextBlock content in the slice and string content at HEAD.

checks.what: Sandbox run 2: hooked report runs with Y: dead, which reads the DriveStatus change (criterion 1)
checks.command: same hook, after silencing the share's server
checks.evidence: Slice run 1: 'drives in ms=2445 held=1909 added=0 buttons=1 labels=1/1 ink=1/1', report buttons=1, exit 0 at +2596 ms. Slice run 2: 'drives in ms=2501 held=1911 buttons=1 labels=1/1', exit 0 at +2699 ms. HEAD: 'refused mode=size reason=the drive buttons did not come in within 20 s', report buttons=0. A Wait/Unknown thread was present only in the dead runs.

checks.what: Sandbox run 2: WM_CLOSE on a no-path launch with Y: alive
checks.command: EnumWindows by pid, PostMessage WM_CLOSE to the window titled 'Filesystem Analyser', inside the Sandbox
checks.evidence: The process exited 36 ms after WM_CLOSE, code 0.

checks.what: Sandbox run 2: WM_CLOSE on a no-path launch with Y: dead (O-014)
checks.command: same, 6 s after launch with the Y: read stuck
checks.evidence: Slice x2: before close there were 19–20 threads, one in Wait/Unknown. 120 s after WM_CLOSE the process was 'STILL RUNNING; 1 threads (Wait/Unknown=1)', and 30 s after Stop-Process it had still not exited. HEAD's exe in the same Sandbox run gave the same result (1 thread, Wait/Unknown; did not exit after the kill). So the behaviour is the same before this slice.

checks.what: Process exit in report mode with a read stuck on the dead share
checks.command: report and hooked report runs above
checks.evidence: Five exits with a stuck Y: read. Slice: 824, 2596 and 2699 ms total, 14–34 ms after the report. HEAD: 723 ms, and 20744 ms, 12 ms after the hook's 20 s refusal. So the shutdown path exits promptly here, but WM_CLOSE did not. The cause of the difference was not established.

checks.what: Underscore labels on an off-screen Button, string vs TextBlock (criterion 11)
checks.command: pwsh -STA .taad-scratch/validate/labeltext.ps1 (Button measured and arranged with no window; visual tree walked)
checks.evidence: string 'WD_BLACK': AccessText=1, key 'B'. TextBlock 'WD_BLACK': AccessText=0, drawn 'D:  WD_BLACK (NTFS)'. string 'USB__DISK': AccessText=1, drawn 'USB_DISK'. TextBlock 'USB__DISK': AccessText=0, drawn 'USB__DISK'. 'OS': no AccessText either way.

checks.what: First version of the off-screen label check (with a Window and an automation peer)
checks.evidence: The engine's guard refused it as operating windows. It was replaced by the window-free layout check above.

Exit 1 in 148 s, 5 FAIL. Scan stalled=true at 333.9 ms, RENDER-PATH. Rescan was also RENDER-PATH, 95% in synchronous render. The trace was read: window start 620.2 ms, plain summary line with no run field. No FSA_* variables were inherited. HEAD stalls the same way (next row).

checks.what: T-005 A/B at 644 px, HEAD copy vs this tree
checks.command: FSA_T005_HEIGHT=644; <root>/tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case T-005 for a git archive of 3ab847c and for this tree
checks.evidence: Both runs passed T-005, exit 0. HEAD: scan max 341.0 ms posted at 579 ms, rescan max 385.2 ms. Slice: scan max 340.3 ms at 576 ms, rescan max 388.8 ms. The SL-080 stall is at HEAD unchanged; the slice neither causes nor fixes it.

criteria.criterion: 1. show the ready drives while one mapped drive does not answer
criteria.how: In the suite, DriveReadsTests passed (A_read_that_does_not_answer_holds_no_other_drive). In a real Sandbox with a dead mapped Y: and the real exe, the slice gave report buttons=1 (C:) and the hook logged 'drives in held=1909/1911 buttons=1'. HEAD gave buttons=0 and the hook refused at 20 s.

criteria.criterion: 2. release the hook's hold only once every answering drive's button is in
criteria.how: The DriveReadsTests FIFO-pump case passed. B-007 read '3 of 3' real buttons over 9 hooked runs. In the Sandbox with Y: alive, the slice logged 'drives in buttons=2 labels=2/2'.

criteria.criterion: 3. add a drive that answers after 'Drives' is shown
criteria.how: Unit level only: DriveReadsTests.A_drive_that_answers_after_the_wait_arrives_on_the_pump passed in the suite. The real Y: never answered during the Sandbox runs, so a late button was not seen in the app.

criteria.criterion: 4. say no drive is ready when none answers in time
criteria.how: The DriveReadsTests case with two reads blocked and a 300 ms bound passed. The two-line 'No ready drives' branch in LoadDrives was read in the diff and not run.

criteria.criterion: 5. skip a drive that is not ready or stops being ready
criteria.how: The DriveReadsTests null-read case passed in the suite.

criteria.criterion: 6. handle a PC with no pickable drive letter
criteria.how: The DriveReadsTests empty-list case passed in the suite.

criteria.criterion: 7. keep the drive buttons in letter order
criteria.how: The DriveReadsTests 2,0,3,1 Place case passed. B-007 passed.

criteria.criterion: 8. surface an unexpected failure while reading drives
9. surface an unexpected failure from a drive that answered late
10. draw each drive's label as written, with no access key (this PC's real drives)
criteria.how: B-007 on this PC: exit 0, labels=3/3 ink=3/3 in every hooked run. The screenshot shows 'C:  OS (NTFS)', 'D:  Samsung 990 Pro (NTFS)' and 'Z:  collab (NTFS)' drawn as written.

criteria.criterion: 11. draw an underscore label such as WD_BLACK or USB_DISK as written
criteria.how: Sandbox with C: labelled WD_BLACK: the slice's real button has TextBlock content (labels=2/2), HEAD's does not (0/2). The off-screen WPF layout gave TextBlock content no AccessText and drew 'WD_BLACK' and 'USB__DISK' as written; string content gave key 'B' and 'USB_DISK'. The drawn WD_BLACK button was not seen and Alt+B was not pressed: the Sandbox has no visible desktop.

criteria.criterion: 12. read a plain T-005 summary in StallStacks
criteria.how: StallStacks -SelfTest PASSED, 14 fixtures. In the startup check, StallStacks with no -Run read a plain summary line with no run field and exited 0.
The self-test passed, including the named, no-stall and unreached shapes. The live startup run reported stalled=true for a 333.9 ms scan wait.

criteria.criterion: 14. show no stall at startup in the existing stall analysis
criteria.how: SL-002-StartupStallStacks.Tests.ps1 exits 1: scan stalled=true at 333.9 ms, RENDER-PATH. HEAD stalls the same way in my A/B (341.0 ms vs 340.3 ms at 644 px). It is pre-existing and was waived as O-013/N-018, but it is not met.

obligations.evidence: Measured in the spike's Sandbox set-up: a mapped Y: whose SMB server was silenced, plus a listener on 445 that never answers. With Y: alive, WM_CLOSE on a no-path launch exited in 36 ms. With Y: dead, WM_CLOSE 6 s after launch left the process alive for 120 s and more, with 1 thread in Wait/Unknown, and Stop-Process had not finished 30 s later. This held for the slice twice and for HEAD's exe once in the same run, so it is pre-existing, not caused by DriveReads. Report-mode Shutdown with the same stuck read exited promptly in all 5 runs (12–34 ms after the report). So the precondition does not hold for window close. Logs: .taad-scratch/sandbox/run-20261117-213436/out/log.txt.

problems.what: Light grey small text on white. It is readable, so the engine's 1.00:1 contrast figure overstates it, but the contrast is low. Pre-existing.

problems.where: strip under the three drive buttons (DriveScroller)
problems.what: A grey horizontal scroll bar with arrows shows although all three buttons fit. It reads as a stray empty bar, and its two arrow buttons are probably the engine's two unnamed Buttons, since the drive buttons carry their labels. Pre-existing.

not_reached: DriveStatus text on a no-path launch: UI Automation found no window in the Sandbox (session 0, window not visible) and is refused on the host. The DriveStatus change was observed only through the hook's 'drives in' line on launches with a path.
Whether a dead-share process left after WM_CLOSE eventually exits once the redirector gives up. Observation was capped at 150 s, so its user impact (a leftover process for minutes) is unmeasured.
Why report-mode Shutdown exits promptly with a stuck read while WM_CLOSE does not. The kernel wait state of the remaining thread was not inspected.
A late-answering drive's button appearing in the real app after 'Drives' (criterion 3): the silenced Y: never answered within any run.
The drawn WD_BLACK / USB__DISK button and the absence of the Alt+B scan, on a visible desktop. No volume on this PC has an underscore, and the Sandbox has no visible window.

Other outage forms: a real sleeping NAS, an offline Tailscale peer such as this PC's Z:\, and a server address that fails the TCP connect slowly (spike N-014). Only an accepted-but-silent loopback SMB endpoint was reproduced.
Windows builds other than 26100.9974 (Sandbox) and 26300 (this PC).
